measurementRule: Do not judge an experiment before a complete comparable 28-day window. Record seven-day values only as leading indicators.

measurementProtocol.restartTrigger: Any search-facing change to the title, description, H1, first answer, structured data, canonical, or indexability resets the window.
measurementProtocol.pendingWindowRule: For pending-clean-window experiments, set releaseDate to the production merge date and evaluate the 28 complete days beginning the next day.
measurementProtocol.parallelExecutionPolicy: Measurement freezes and stop-loss actions are page-specific, not site-wide. Stop or roll back an affected experiment, then continue one non-overlapping reversible experiment on unaffected pages or distribution surfaces.
measurementProtocol.powerFloorRule: Do not freeze a page for a CTR experiment unless its 28-day baseline clears BOTH 4,000 impressions and 80 clicks. Below that floor a 28-day window cannot resolve even a 50% relative CTR change, so the freeze costs shipping speed and buys nothing. Measured 2026-09-01 across 21 experiments: only /northern-lights-michigan/ and /soo-locks/ cleared it. Everything else needed between 2,229 and 77,988 impressions per arm to detect a 50% lift against baselines of 30 to 5,479. For pages under the floor, measure average position and impressions instead, which carry far more data and move first, or simply ship and watch rank.
measurementProtocol.partialReadRule: A window may be closed early when the remaining days cannot change the decision. Record readType partial-window, the elapsed days, and the detectable difference at read time. This is not licence to peek and stop when a number looks good: decide the read date before looking.
measurementProtocol.seasonalityCaveat: Window length does not protect a seasonal or event-driven page. Aurora impressions are driven by geomagnetic storms and news cycles, and fall pages by the season itself. Check the daily impression curve for spikes before trusting any aggregate, whether partial or complete.
